title: Hanuma enters the city of Lanka
introduction: Entering Lanka at night by placing His left foot desiring the destruction of enemies, Hanuma hears various musical instruments being played upon inside. He also observes enemies' forces and moves towards the royal gynaeceum.
closing: Thus, this is the 4th chapter in Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
स निर्जत्य पुरीम् लण्का श्रेष्ठाम् ताम् कामरूपिणीम् |
विक्रमेण महातेजा हनुमान् कपिसत्तमः
अद्वारेण मःआतेजा हौमान् कपिसत्तमः |
verses.iast:
sa nirjatya purīm laṇkā śreśhṭhām tām kāmarūpiṇīm |
vikrameṇa mahātejā hanumān kapisattamaḥ
advāreṇa maḥātejā haumān kapisattamaḥ |
verses.translation: That Hanuma the best among Vanaras, the great radiant one, the long armed one, conquered with His might the best Lanka who is capable of assuming desired form. He then leapt over the city wall at a place that was not a gate.

verses.devanagari:
प्रविश्य नगरीम् लङ्काम् कपिराजहितम्करः
चक्रेणाऽथ पदम् सव्यम् शत्रूणाम् स तु मूर्धनि |
verses.iast:
praviśya nagarīm laṇ^kām kapirājahitamkaraḥ
cakreṇā'tha padam savyam śatrūṇām sa tu mūrdhani |
verses.translation: Desiring the benefit of the king of Vanaras Sugreeva, that Hanuma entered the city of Lanka and thus actually placed His left foot on the enemies' heads.
notes: Comment : When entering a city of enemies, one who wishes their destruction should always place one's left foot first into the city.

glosses.meaning: desiring the benefit of the king of Vanaras

verses.devanagari:
प्रविष्टः सत्त्वसंपन्नो विशायाम् मारुतात्मजः
स महापथमास्थाय मुक्तापुष्पविराजितम् |
ततस्तु ताम् पुरीम् लङ्काम् रम्यामभिययौ कपिः
verses.iast:
praviśhṭaḥ sattvasampanno viśāyām mārutātmajaḥ
sa mahāpathamāsthāya muktāpuśhpavirājitam |
tatastu tām purīm laṇ^kām ramyāmabhiyayau kapiḥ
verses.translation: That son of Vayu endowed with great strength, entered the city at night and took the grand road shone by flowers and pearls. After that Hanuma went towards that beautiful city of Lanka.

glosses.meaning: towards that beautiful city of Lanka.

verses.devanagari:
हसित उद्घुष्ट निनदैः तूर्य घोष पुरः सरैः |
वज्र अन्कुश निकाशैः च वज्र जाल विभूषितैः
गृह मेधैः पुरी रम्या बभासे द्यौः इव अम्बुदैः |
verses.iast:
hasita udghuṣṭa ninadaiḥ tūrya ghoṣa puraḥ saraiḥ |
vajra ankuśa nikāśaiḥ ca vajra jāla vibhūṣitaiḥ
gṛha medhaiḥ purī ramyā babhāse dyauḥ iva ambudaiḥ |
verses.translation: The beautiful city shone like the sky together with clouds, with its cloud like houses filled with sounds of laughter and with sounds of musical instruments at the interior, equal in strength to diamonds and clubs and with windows decorated with diamonds.

glosses.meaning: with sounds of musical instruments at the interior
equal (in strength) to diamonds and clubs

verses.devanagari:
प्रजज्वाल तदा लन्का रक्षः गण गृहैः शुभैः
सित अभ्र सदृशैः चित्रैः पद्म स्वस्तिक संस्थितैः |
वर्धमान गृहैः च अपि सर्वतः सुविभाषितैः
verses.iast:
prajajvāla tadā lankā rakṣaḥ gaṇa gṛhaiḥ śubhaiḥ
sita abhra sadṛśaiḥ citraiḥ padma svastika saṃsthitaiḥ |
vardhamāna gṛhaiḥ ca api sarvataḥ suvibhāṣitaiḥ
verses.translation: Then that city of Lanka shone brilliantly being well decorated by the houses of Rakshasas. These were modern houses which equalled white clouds, which were surprising with the shape of lotus and swastika and which were auspicious.

glosses.meaning: with the shape of lotus and swastika

verses.devanagari:
ताम् चित्र माल्य आभरणाम् कपि राज हितम् करः |
राघव अर्थम् चरन् श्रीमान् ददर्श च ननन्द च
verses.iast:
tām citra mālya ābharaṇām kapi rāja hitam karaḥ |
rāghava artham caran śrīmān dadarśa ca nananda ca
verses.translation: That glorious Hanuma, performer of beneficial deeds for Sugreeva the king of monkeys, moved around the city of Lanka which had wonderful garlands and jewellery, for the sake of Sri Rama. He saw the city and became happy too.

glosses.meaning: performer of good deeds for the king of monkeys
for the sake of Sri Rama

verses.devanagari:
भवनाद्भवनं गच्छ्न् ददर्श पवनात्मजः |
विविधाकृतिरूपाणि भवनानि ततस्ततः
verses.iast:
bhavanādbhavanaṃ gacchn dadarśa pavanātmajaḥ |
vividhākṛtirūpāṇi bhavanāni tatastataḥ
verses.translation: Going from one building to another, Hanuma saw buildings in various shapes and forms on every side.

verses.devanagari:
शुश्राव मधुरम् गीतम् त्रि स्थान स्वर भूषितम् |
स्त्रीणाम् मद समृद्धानाम् दिवि च अप्सरसाम् इव
verses.iast:
śuśrāva madhuram gītam tri sthāna svara bhūṣitam |
strīṇām mada samṛddhānām divi ca apsarasām iva
verses.translation: Hanuma heard a sweet song which was decorated by sound from the three svaras - Mandra, Madhya and Tara of love lorne women like Apsara women in heaven.

glosses.meaning: decorated by sounds born from the three areas- Mandra

verses.devanagari:
शुश्राव कान्ची निनदम् नूपुराणाम् च निह्स्वनम् |
सोपान निनदामः चैव भवनेषु महात्मनम्
verses.iast:
śuśrāva kāncī ninadam nūpurāṇām ca nihsvanam |
sopāna ninadāmḥ caiva bhavaneṣu mahātmanam
verses.translation: Hanuma also heard there and there sound from the tinkling of ornaments worn around the waist in the houses of wealthy people, sounds of footfall over stair, sound from clapping of arms by warriors and roar of ogres.

glosses.meaning: tinkling of ornaments worn around the waist
sound from warriors due to clapping of arms

verses.devanagari:
आस्फोटित निनादामः च क्ष्वेडितामः च ततः ततः |
शुश्राव जपताम् तत्र मन्त्रन् रक्षोगृहेषु वै
verses.iast:
āsphoṭita ninādāmḥ ca kṣveḍitāmḥ ca tataḥ tataḥ |
śuśrāva japatām tatra mantran rakśogṛheśhu vai
verses.translation: Hanuma also heard there and there sound from the tinkling of ornaments worn around the waist in the houses of wealthy people, sounds of footfall over stair, sound from clapping of arms by warriors and roar of ogres.

glosses.meaning: tinkling of ornaments worn around the waist
sound from warriors due to clapping of arms

verses.devanagari:
स्वाध्याय निरतामः चैव यातु धानान् ददर्श सः |
रावण स्तव सम्युक्तान् गर्जतः राक्षसान् अपि
verses.iast:
svādhyāya niratāmḥ caiva yātu dhānān dadarśa saḥ |
rāvaṇa stava samyuktān garjataḥ rākṣasān api
verses.translation: There Hanuma heard ritual chantings muttered by rakshasas in their houses. He saw ogres engaged in study of Vedas. He also saw roaring rakshasas who came together to praise Ravana.

glosses.meaning: who came together praise to Ravana.

verses.devanagari:
राज मार्गम् समावृत्य स्थितम् रक्षः बलम् महत् |
ददर्श मध्यमे गुल्मे राक्षसस्य चरान् बहून्
verses.iast:
rāja mārgam samāvṛtya sthitam rakṣaḥ balam mahat |
dadarśa madhyame gulme rākṣasasya carān bahūn
verses.translation: He saw many spies of Ravana and a big army of ogres which stood surrounding the royal highway in the central zone of city.

glosses.meaning: in the central zone of the city.

verses.devanagari:
दीक्षितान् जटिलान् मुण्डान् गः अजिन अम्बर वाससः |
दर्भ मुष्टि प्रहरणान् अग्नि कुण्ड आयुधामः तथा
कूट मुद्गर पाणीमः च दण्ड आयुध धरान् अपि |
एक अक्ष अनेक कर्णामः च चलल् लम्ब पयः धरान्
करालान् भुग्न वक्त्रामः च विकटान् वामनामः तथा |
धन्विनः खड्गिनः चैव शतघ्नी मुसल आयुधान्
परिघ उत्तम हस्तामः च विचित्र कवच उज्ज्वलान् |
नातिस्थूलान् नातिकृशान् नातिदीर्घ अतिह्रस्वकान्
नातिगौरान्नातिकृष्णान्नातिकुब्जान्न वामनान् |
विरूपान् बहु रूपामः च सुरूपामः च सुवर्चसः
verses.iast:
dīkṣitān jaṭilān muṇḍān gaḥ ajina ambara vāsasaḥ |
darbha muṣṭi praharaṇān agni kuṇḍa āyudhāmḥ tathā
kūṭa mudgara pāṇīmḥ ca daṇḍa āyudha dharān api |
eka akṣa aneka karṇāmḥ ca calal lamba payaḥ dharān
karālān bhugna vaktrāmḥ ca vikaṭān vāmanāmḥ tathā |
dhanvinaḥ khaḍginaḥ caiva śataghnī musala āyudhān
parigha uttama hastāmḥ ca vicitra kavaca ujjvalān |
nātisthūlān nātikṛśān nātidīrgha atihrasvakān
nātigaurānnātikṛśhṇānnātikubjānna vāmanān |
virūpān bahu rūpāmḥ ca surūpāmḥ ca suvarcasaḥ
verses.translation: Hanuma saw those who were initiated into various Vedic practices, those who wore matted locks on their head, those who had shaven heads, those who wore cow hides and other clothing, those who were carrying Kusa grass as weapons and also those who had fire vessels as weapons, those who carried hammers and clubs in their hands and also those who had worn staffs as weapons, hose who were one-eyed, those who had one ear, hose who were pot-bellied and with hanging breast, those who had horrible appearances, those with twisted mouths, those who were horrific and also short people, those who carried bows and arrows those who carried swords, those who carried pestles and clubs as weapons, those who carried excellent Parighas in their hands, those who shone with strange armour, those who were not very fat, those who were not too thin, those who were neither tall nor short, those who were not very fair, those who were not very dark, those who were not very hunchbacked, those who were not very short, those who had great brilliance, those who carried banners, those who carried flags and those who carried different weapons.

glosses.meaning: those who were initiated into various Vedic practices
those who wore matted locks on their head
those who had worn cow hides and other clothing
those who were carrying Kusa grass as weapons
those who had fire vessels as weapons
those who carried hammers and clubs in their hands
and also those who had worn staffs as weapons
those who were pot-bellied and with hanging breast
those who carried bows and arrows
those who carried pestles and clubs as weapons
those who carried excellent Parighas in their hands
those who shone with strange armour
those who were not very fat
those who were not too thin
those who were neither tall nor short
those who were not very fair
those who were not very dark
those who were not very hunchbacked
those who were not very short
those who had a good appearance

verses.devanagari:
ध्वजीन् पताकिनश्चैव ददर्श विविधायुधान् |
शक्ति वृक्ष आयुधामः चैव पट्टिश अशनि धारिणः
क्षेपणी पाश हस्तामः च ददर्श स महा कपिः |
स्रग्विणः त्व् अनुलिप्तामः च वर आभरण भूषितान्
नानावेषसमायुक्तान्यथास्वैरगतान् बहून् |
तीक्ष्ण शूल धरामः चैव वज्रिणः च महा बलान् | |
verses.iast:
dhvajīn patākinaścaiva dadarśa vividhāyudhān |
śakti vṛkṣa āyudhāmḥ caiva paṭṭiśa aśani dhāriṇaḥ
kṣepaṇī pāśa hastāmḥ ca dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ |
sragviṇaḥ tv anuliptāmḥ ca vara ābharaṇa bhūṣitān
nānāveśhasamāyuktānyathāsvairagatān bahūn |
tīkṣṇa śūla dharāmḥ caiva vajriṇaḥ ca mahā balān | |
verses.translation: Hanuma saw many people, who had great might, who carried javelins and trees as weapons, those who carried Pattisas and thunderbolts, those who carried in their hands sling and nooses, those who carried flowered garlands, wearing sandal paste and decorated with best jewellery, those who had various kinds of appearances roaming freely at will, those who carried sharp spikes and thunderbolts.

glosses.meaning: those who carried javelins and trees as weapons
and holding a sling and noose in their hands

verses.devanagari:
शत साहस्रम् अव्यग्रम् आरक्षम् मध्यमम् कपिः |
रक्षोधिपतिनिर्दिष्टम् ददर्शान्तःपुराग्रतः || |
verses.iast:
śata sāhasram avyagram ārakṣam madhyamam kapiḥ |
rakśodhipatinirdiśhṭam dadarśāntaḥpurāgrataḥ || |
verses.translation: Hanuma saw at the front of inner city, a hundred thousand central protective force which was attentive and was positioned there at the command of Ravana.

glosses.meaning: positioned at the command of Ravana.

verses.devanagari:
स तदा तद्गृहम् दृष्ट्वा महाहाटकतोरणम् |
राक्षसेन्द्रस्य विख्यातमद्रिमूर्ध्नि प्रतिष्ठितम्
पुण्डरीकावतंसाभिः परिखाभिरलम्कृतम् |
प्राकार आवृतम् अत्यन्तम् ददर्श स महा कपिः
verses.iast:
sa tadā tadgṛham dṛśhṭvā mahāhāṭakatoraṇam |
rākśasendrasya vikhyātamadrimūrdhni pratiśhṭhitam
puṇḍarīkāvataṃsābhiḥ parikhābhiralamkṛtam |
prākāra āvṛtam atyantam dadarśa sa mahā kapiḥ
verses.translation: That Hanuma saw Ravana's house with a golden doorway. That famed house was on the top of a mountain. Motes filled with white lotuses surrounded it. It was also surrounded by a compound wall. He watched the house again and again.

verses.devanagari:
त्रिविष्टप निभम् दिव्यम् दिव्य नाद विनादितम् |
वाजि हेषित सम्घुष्टम् नादितम् भूषणैः तथा
रथैः यानैः विमानैः च तथा गज हयैः शुभैः |
वारणैः च चतुः दन्तैः श्वेत अभ्र निचय उपमैः
भूषितम् रुचिर द्वारम् मत्तैः च मृग पक्षिभिः |
राक्षस अधिपतेः गुप्तम् आविवेश गृहम् कपिः
verses.iast:
triviṣṭapa nibham divyam divya nāda vināditam |
vāji heṣita samghuṣṭam nāditam bhūṣaṇaiḥ tathā
rathaiḥ yānaiḥ vimānaiḥ ca tathā gaja hayaiḥ śubhaiḥ |
vāraṇaiḥ ca catuḥ dantaiḥ śveta abhra nicaya upamaiḥ
bhūṣitam rucira dvāram mattaiḥ ca mṛga pakṣibhiḥ |
rākṣasa adhipateḥ guptam āviveśa gṛham kapiḥ
verses.translation: The great Hanuma entered secretly Ravana's inner city which was equal to paradise, rendered noisy by neighing of horses and tinkling of ornaments, by chariots, vehicles and aerial-cars and decorated by auspicious elephants and horses and great elephants with four tusks and by birds and animals in heat. It had beautiful entrances and was protected by thousands of rakshasas with great strength.

glosses.meaning: equalling a group of white clouds

verses.devanagari:
सहेमजाम्बूनदचक्रवाळम् |
महार्ह मुक्तामणिभूषितान्तम् |
परार्थ्यकालागुरुचन्दनाक्तं |
स रावणान्तःपुरमाविवेश
verses.iast:
sahemajāmbūnadacakravāLam |
mahārha muktāmaṇibhūśhitāntam |
parārthyakālāgurucandanāktaṃ |
sa rāvaṇāntḥpuramāviveśa
verses.translation: Hanuma entered the inner city of Ravana which was filled with gold, which had a golden court-yard , with a central area decorated by pearls and diamonds of great value and sprinkled daily with water containing superb algallocum and sandal-wood.

glosses.meaning: the in inner city of Ravana
with a central area decorated by pearls and diamonds of great value
and which was sprinkled with water containing superb agallocum and sandal-wood.
